correctness.rationale: The degree-five integer polynomial P_k has 5 simple roots isolated by 330 disjoint exact rational radius-10^-6 Rouche disks. For each k 0..65 the strictly smallest-modulus root is real positive with positive residue, and strict root/residue bounds guarantee its dominance for all n>=300. Independently recomputed 330 root centers using high-precision numerical candidates then checked all root-disk, simple-pole and tail inequalities using only exact rational bounds; the largest competing-pole/positive-residue ratio at n=300 was 0.3376494235153464<17/50. Separately evaluated 19,734 exact positive finite coefficients (n=1..299) and negative c_38(66,5). Thus the all-n statement uses a proven tail bound, not extrapolation of a finite run. The certificate script and data at exact pinned paths were inspected.
